brief.headline: Close the ₹28.69 L annual price gap to our best suppliers, leveraging our 47.43% share of their revenue and credible alternates.

priceAsk.summary: Benchmark Cincorp's prices to Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic — our current best suppliers for the same items.
priceAsk.target: ₹28.69 L annual saving by closing the price gap
priceAsk.basis: Three top SKUs show we overpay: PP CAP at ₹1.08/NOS vs ₹0.81/NOS (33.2% gap, ₹14.05 L excess), HDPE BOT at ₹1.53/NOS vs ₹1.38/NOS (10.7%, ₹7.88 L), and MESU. CUP at ₹0.46/NOS vs ₹0.35/NOS (30.6%, ₹6.75 L). We already pay these lower prices to Mars Plastics and Premier Plastic for comparable rigid plastic packaging.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 Days After Receipt to 30 days, releasing ₹16.02 L working capital for us.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹16.02 L working capital freed if we shift to 30-day terms; a further ₹8.01 L at 15 days more (net 15)

brief.financialLeverage: Cincorp earns a 6.0% net margin versus the 15.0% peer median — less than half — so they have limited cushion for price cuts. Their 11.5% return on capital trails the 15.3% peer median. They carry debt at 1.13x debt-to-equity and a 4.54% effective borrowing cost. Our ₹1.95 Cr annual spend is 47.43% of their ₹4.11 Cr revenue, making us a critical customer they cannot afford to lose. Their Altman Z-score of 1.83 sits in the grey zone (distress watch) and free cash flow is ₹-79.14 L, signalling tight liquidity. Push firmly on price to close the ₹28.69 L gap, but frame it around volume retention and offer faster payment (worth 4.54% to them) in return — a hard squeeze risks tipping a fragile supplier.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹28.69 L per year versus the best prices we already secure from other suppliers for the same rigid plastic packaging items.
Our annual spend of ₹1.95 Cr represents 47.43% of Cincorp's total ₹4.11 Cr revenue — we are their largest customer by far.
Cincorp's 6.0% net margin is less than half the 15.0% peer median, leaving little room for discounting without stress.
They stretch their own supplier payments to 39 days versus a 23-day peer median, so asking them to tighten our receivable window is consistent with industry practice.
Their Altman Z-score of 1.83 places them in the grey zone — a supply-continuity watch — and negative free cash flow of ₹-79.14 L signals cash stress.
On the PP CAP PLAS 28MM SKU alone, we pay ₹1.08/NOS when Mars Plastics supplies it at ₹0.81/NOS — a 33.2% premium costing us ₹14.05 L annually.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter with ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B (65/100), and proven capability in pharma bottles, caps, and closures — the strongest second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader with ₹946.50 Cr revenue and health score A (79/100); supplies pails, containers, and pharma packaging — a robust, financially stable alternate for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Mars Plastics
alternates.why: Already our best-price supplier on two of the top three SKUs (PP CAP at ₹0.81/NOS and HDPE BOT at ₹1.38/NOS) — a proven, price-competitive source we can shift more volume to immediately.

risks: Cincorp's 1.83 Altman Z-score (grey zone) and ₹-79.14 L negative free cash flow mean financial distress is a real risk — pushing too hard on price without offering payment relief could trigger supply disruption.

We represent 47.43% of their revenue; if we walk, their viability is in question — frame the negotiation as partnership (volume retention, faster payment) rather than a hard squeeze that forces them into a corner.

Their 6.0% net margin (vs 15.0% peer median) leaves almost no fat to cut — prioritise the highest-gap SKUs (PP CAP 33.2%, MESU. CUP 30.6%) rather than across-the-board cuts, and trade payment speed for price where possible.

Small entity under ₹10 Cr with a C (51/100) health score — verify production capacity and quality consistency before shifting significant volume, and qualify Manjushree or Mold-Tek in parallel to derisk.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹28.69 lakh more per year than our best suppliers for the same items — let's work together to close that gap and secure the volume for the long term.
